name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT

  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.
Platform: iPadOS. Report editor footer has four equally prominent filled buttons: Publish, Preview, Save Draft and Delete. Delete is the primary/default action. Glyph-only Preview has no accessible name. Every hit region is 20x20 pt with 2 pt gaps. During an 8-second Publish upload nothing changes and repeated taps create duplicate uploads. Product requirement: preserve all four functions. No rendered app or runtime is supplied.

# Apple HIG: menus and actions

Separate direct actions from state selection and navigation, then choose a discoverable primary surface plus contextual shortcuts. Use menu-bar commands as the full catalog on Mac, keep high-value toolbar actions visible, and preserve standard roles and labels. Read component-specific platform rules: menus, share extensions, toolbar placement, targeting sizes, and destructive confirmations vary.

Start with accessibility, inclusion, and privacy constraints that affect the whole experience. # Buttons Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Style](#Style) - [Content](#Content) - [Role](#Role) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) A button performs an immediate action. Its visual style, visible symbol/text, and semantic role work together to explain what activation does. ## Best practices Allow enough surrounding space for clear separation and easy selection. General hit regions should be at least 44×44 pt; visionOS targets need 60×60 pt. Custom buttons always need press feedback. ## Style Prefer system styles for built-in states, accessibility, and appearance adaptation. Use one or two prominent buttons per view for likely actions. Distinguish a preferred option through style rather than making related buttons different sizes. Keep label colors distinct from colorful content; the default monochrome often works best over rich backgrounds. ## Content Use a familiar symbol for a familiar action; use a short title-case verb phrase when words are clearer. Mac and visionOS can provide brief hover tooltips; text-labeled buttons usually explain themselves. ## Role Normal has no special meaning; primary is the expected/default action; Cancel abandons the current action; destructive signals data loss. Roles affect rendering, such as accent fill for primary and red for destructive. Primary can respond to Return and close a temporary view. Generally assign primary only to a nondestructive likely action. Application advice: consult the alert-specific deliberate-destruction exception before prescribing confirmation behavior. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS For delayed completion, show an activity indicator within the activating button, optionally changing its label to the current operation. The indicator replaces any button image while preserving context for the wait. ### macOS #### Push buttons The standard push button can show text, imagery, or both and can serve as default. Use flexible height for tall icons or multiple text lines, otherwise retain standard sizing. Append an ellipsis when the button opens another window/view/app for further input. Consider spring loading through a dragged selection plus force-click on Magic Trackpad, preserving the drag afterward. #### Square buttons These small glyph-only controls affect a nearby view, for example adding/removing table rows. They can act as push, toggle, or pop-up controls. Use them in the body rather than the frame, toolbar, or status bar. Prefer system symbols and omit introductory labels when proximity explains the function. #### Help buttons Use the familiar system question-mark control, at most one per window, opening context-specific help when possible and top-level help otherwise. In a dialog with dismissal controls, place it in the opposite lower corner, aligned vertically with those controls. Without dismissal controls, or in settings, use either lower corner. Keep it in the view body and omit explanatory introductory text. #### Image buttons Image buttons can act as push, toggle, or pop-up controls inside a view. Toolbar imagery instead belongs to a toolbar item. Allow about 10 pixels between image and clickable button edges and generally omit a visible system border. Put any needed label beneath the image. ### visionOS Buttons normally have a visible background and audible feedback. Circle suits glyph-only content, rounded rectangle or capsule suits text, and capsule suits text plus glyph. Standard states supply feedback; custom hover effects are not supported. A look-triggered tooltip can explain a glyph. | Shape | Supported visual sizes | | --- | --- | | Circle | Mini 28 pt; small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt; extra large 64 pt | | Text capsule | Small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | | Text-and-icon capsule | Regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | | Rounded rectangle | Small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | Visual size does not remove the 60-pt targeting requirement. Use a discernible shape/fill except inside a larger clearly bounded toolbar, menu, alert, or ornament. On window glass, thin material suits the button; floating in space, use glass. Reserve white fill with black content for the system's toggled state. Prefer round/capsule forms for steady gaze, and a capsule for a standalone button. Keep centers at least 60 pt apart; add 4 pt padding around buttons 60 pt or larger to prevent hover overlap. Avoid rows/stacks of mini/small buttons. Prefer rounded rectangles for vertical text stacks and capsules for horizontal rows. Standard sounds matter because visionOS provides no haptics. ### watchOS Inline buttons are capsules with a contrasting material. Put corner actions in a toolbar so the system relocates title/time and gives controls Liquid Glass. Full-width buttons suit primary actions. Side-by-side buttons should share height and use short labels or glyphs; vertical one- and two-line buttons should also maintain common heights. Toolbar actions can navigate related areas or operate on current content. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Pop-up buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pop-up-buttons) [Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons) [Toggles](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles) [Segmented controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls) [Location button](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Location-button) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: December 16, 2025, June 9, 2025, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023, June 5, 2023. # Progress indicators Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Progress UI is temporary feedback during work, disappearing when it finishes. Determinate indicators represent measurable completion with a leading-to-trailing bar or clockwise circular fill. Indeterminate indicators communicate ongoing activity without a completion estimate; every platform has a spinner, and macOS also has an indeterminate bar. ## Best practices Prefer measurable progress when possible and report it honestly. Estimate the whole operation so an early sprint to 90% does not conceal a much longer final stage. Keep activity visibly ongoing, and explain stalls with a useful recovery route. When duration becomes known, an indeterminate bar can become determinate; avoid changing a spinner into a differently shaped bar midtask because that disrupts layout and interpretation. Add a short, specific task description only when it supplies real context. Choose a consistent place for status. Allow cancellation where it is safe; offer pause as well when cancel would discard useful partial work. Explain consequential cancellation and let the person either confirm it or resume. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or visionOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS #### Refresh content controls Pull-to-refresh reveals an activity indicator when people drag down a content view. It supplements periodic automatic refreshes rather than making users responsible for every update. An optional title should convey useful content context, such as the previous update time, rather than explaining the pull gesture or merely restating that loading is occurring. ### macOS Both animated bars and spinners can represent indeterminate work. Prefer a small spinner for asynchronous background operations or tight spaces, such as beside a control or within a field. Usually omit spinner labels when the initiating action already explains the activity. ### watchOS Progress bars, circular fills, and spinners default to white against the scene background. Tint can customize their color. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — UIKit — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 12, 2023, June 5, 2023. # Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

Choose presentation from urgency, scope, duration, and whether the parent must remain usable. Reserve alerts for critical actionable interruptions; sheets for scoped tasks; popovers and panels for contextual tools; windows for sustained parallel work. # Alerts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. An alert interrupts to communicate urgent, critical information and useful actions, including problems, unexpected data loss, or important confirmations. ## Best practices Reserve alerts for situations that warrant immediate attention. Put informational status in context when no action is required. Common undoable deletions generally need no confirmation; uncommon irreversible destruction does. Avoid startup alerts: cached or placeholder content with a discreet problem explanation is often a better response to an unavailable network. ## Anatomy Alerts are modal and adapt their appearance to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS rather than using one universal layout. ## Content Use a title, optional message, and up to three buttons. iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS can include text fields; macOS and visionOS can include an icon and accessory view. macOS additionally supports a suppression checkbox and Help button. Use direct, neutral, approachable wording without blaming the person or concealing severity. The title should explain what happened, its context, and cause as concisely as possible, generally within two lines. Avoid a bare error label or code. Complete-sentence titles use sentence case and punctuation; fragments use title case without punctuation. Additional text should add information in brief complete sentences. Clear action labels should make button explanations unnecessary; if instructions are unavoidable, use device-neutral language such as choose and the exact title without quotation marks. Include an input field only when resolving the situation requires it, with secure entry for passwords. ## Buttons Use short, usually one- or two-word, title-case action labels without punctuation. Prefer specific outcomes over Yes/No or ambiguous OK; reserve OK for purely informational acknowledgment. A cancellation action is always Cancel. Place the expected/default action at the trailing end of a row or top of a stack, with cancellation generally leading or at the bottom. Apply destructive styling to destructive consequences the person did not deliberately request. A confirmation of an explicitly chosen destruction, such as Empty Trash, can retain a normal default action so Return confirms intent. Always provide Cancel alongside destructive actions, but do not make Cancel the default. To force a deliberate reading, consider no default. A single default acknowledgment button should be Done rather than Cancel. Support familiar alternate cancellation where appropriate: Home Screen exit on iOS/iPadOS; Escape or Command-Period on attached keyboards in iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS; Menu on the tvOS remote. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use action sheets for multiple choices following an intentional action. Keep titles and optional messages short to minimize scrolling, while accommodating enlarged accessibility text. ### macOS The app icon appears automatically but can be replaced. Repeating alerts can offer suppression; necessary details can use an accessory view, and Help can open documentation. Reserve a caution symbol for situations needing extra attention, particularly unexpected loss, rather than routine overwrite, save, or empty-trash tasks. ### visionOS In Shared Space, an alert sits slightly in front of its parent window and stays attached when the window moves. In Full Space, it centers in the wearer's field of view. An accessory view must be no taller than 154 pt and use a 16-pt corner radius. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: February 2, 2024, September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

item.text: The specification confirms five issues: duplicate uploads, undersized targets, an unnamed Preview control, Delete as the default, and four competing prominent buttons. I’ll make Publish the sole prominent action and define upload feedback and duplicate prevention separately. The deletion plan will remain conditional because the supplied file doesn’t say whether deletion is reversible.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > result.md <<'EOF'
# iPad report editor export-control correction plan

This is a specification audit of [interface.md](interface.md), not an execution audit. Preserve Publish, Preview, Save Draft, and Delete. All four remain direct, discoverable footer actions; no Apple SDK is assumed.

## Ranked verified findings

Priority reflects likely harm and task blockage; it is a product judgment, not an Apple severity scale. “Verified” means explicitly stated in interface.md.

| Rank | Observed evidence and effect | Correction and guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — High | During the eight-second Publish upload, nothing changes and repeat taps create duplicate uploads. People cannot tell whether activation worked and can accidentally publish repeatedly. | Immediately show an activity indicator inside Publish, replacing any image, with “Publishing…”; prevent additional submissions while active. HIG explicitly describes in-button activity for delayed iOS/iPadOS actions; duplicate prevention is the engineering decision that makes this safe. [Buttons: iOS, iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#iOS-iPadOS), [Progress: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators#Best-practices). |
| 2 — High | Delete is the primary/default action. A dangerous operation receives the expected-action emphasis and default activation. Actual deletion reversibility and keyboard behavior are unknown. | Remove Delete’s primary/default role; give it destructive semantics and a clear text label. Make Publish the preferred nondestructive footer action. [Buttons: role](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Role). |
| 3 — High | Every hit region is 20 × 20 pt, with 2 pt gaps. These targets are below both locally documented iPadOS size references and are tightly packed. | Use hit regions at least 44 × 44 pt, with clear separation and no overlap. Adopt 12 pt edge-to-edge gaps as this plan’s starting layout value, to validate at actual sizes. [Buttons: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Best-practices), [Accessibility: mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Mobility). |
| 4 — High | Glyph-only Preview has no accessible name. Its purpose is unavailable through its name to assistive interaction. | Display “Preview” and expose accessible name “Preview” and button semantics. If a glyph is retained, treat it as decorative alongside that label. [Buttons: content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Content), [Accessibility: vision and mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision). |
